chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Make them from the four.' Safwan ibn Yahya said to him, 'For precaution,' and he said, 'Yes.' As for the dowry in mut'ah (temporary marriage), it is what they mutually agree upon, whether little or much.

key_terms.الِاحْتِيَاطِ: Precaution (often used in fiqh to indicate a safer legal ruling)
key_terms.الْمَهْرُ: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةِ: Temporary marriage (mut'ah), a specific form of marriage in Shia fiqh
key_terms.صَفْوَانُ بْنُ يَحْيَى: A prominent narrator known for his careful transmission of hadith

ai.seo_question: What is the rule for determining the dowry in temporary marriage (mut'ah) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the dowry (mahr) in temporary marriage (mut'ah) is entirely subject to mutual agreement, regardless of whether it is small or large. The reference to 'the four' likely alludes to the essential components of the contract discussed in preceding narrations, while Safwan ibn Yahya’s query highlights the scholarly practice of applying precaution (ihtiyat) in legal rulings. This underscores the flexibility of mut'ah contracts within Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing them from permanent marriage requirements.
